PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

CLOSED, NOT LOWERED. This floor read 3226 against 3220 for a long time, and the six were ten new files that gave the `// @ts-check` pragma back plus three that moved. They are annotated rather than absorbed.

THE FLOOR MOVES DOWN PAST ITS OWN VALUE and that is not a paydown to spend elsewhere: the gate counts files WITHOUT the pragma, so annotating a file that predates the floor lowers it too. Seven of the thirteen were already under 3220.

WHY IT SAT RED. Annotating a file surfaces whatever it was hiding, and `tsc` carries its own exact floor at 1484 -- so the obvious move is to bank a tsc regression to close a jstscheck one, which is one improvement paying for another and is what CLAUDE.md section 9.2 warns a floor note must never hide. Seven errors appeared and all seven are resolved at their cause. tsc measures 1484 before and after, verified both ways.

  five were ONE defect two levels up. EmployeeFieldRelationMixin (`@param { Class }`) and WithUserChatter (a parameter widened to `typeof Component`) erased what they wrapped, so every member of every wrapped class was invisible to every subclass -- `getTagProps` is declared three levels up on Many2ManyTagsAvatarField. Both now take a constrained `@template` with an INFERRED return, which restores type information for every consumer of either mixin rather than only for the annotated file. They were the only `@param { Class }` in addons/.
  one was a vendored bundle: `import("joint")` against a directory in tsconfig `exclude`. Ambient declaration on the o-spreadsheet precedent, which works with the exclusion where a `paths` entry would defeat it.
  one was a POS server-loaded field. Interface merging, zero emitted code; a class field would have overwritten the loaded value at construction.
  one `@override` tag was REMOVED rather than fixed. TS will not confirm an override through a mixin-produced base, `noImplicitOverride` is off, and the neighbouring override of the same method carries none. That one is a documentation claim, not a code defect, and calling it an architectural fix would be dressing it up.

Measured in a clean detached worktree at the commit this stamps, dirty count 0. Every changed line in the fifteen existing files is a comment and the two new files are `.d.ts`, so the runtime is provably unchanged and no suite can distinguish the commit from its parent.

PREVIOUS NOTE, kept because a floor that loses its history costs more than the stamp gains:

Opened at 3213, measured with the CI command (`python tooling/architecture/js_ts_check.py
--count`) at HEAD on a clean detached worktree.

The unit is FILES under a `static/src` of `addons/` carrying no `// @ts-check`
in their leading comment run, after the ignore list in `eslint.config.mjs` is
applied. 852 of the 4,065 scanned files carry the directive; 3,213 do not.

Debt rather than a contract, and the argument for the floor is that the
alternative measures nothing: `tsconfig.json` sets `allowJs` with `strict`,
`noImplicitAny` and `strictNullChecks` all false, so a file without the
directive is parsed and believed and contributes zero to `tsc.json`. Deleting a
directive therefore lowers no existing floor, and adding one to a dirty file
raises `tsc` by the errors it was already hiding -- which is why this number and
`tsc` move in opposite directions and neither can stand in for the other.

Per scope on the same tree: web 2, stock 45, account 78, point_of_sale 171,
mail 397. None is zero, so none is onboarded as a hard zero yet. web`s two are
`module_loader.js` (the pre-loader IIFE, which runs before the module system)
and `service_worker.js` (measured by tsc_serviceworker against lib.webworker),
both first committed in 2023 and neither an artifact of the web_enterprise
fold.
